ex.ja: 医師達はいくつかの驚くべき事実を発見した。

en: Striving; earnest endeavor; hard work.
Exertion or contention for superiority, either by physical or intellectual means.

strife.ety: From Middle English strif, stryf, striffe, from Old French estrif, noun derived from estriver, from Frankish *strīban; compare Dutch strijven. More at strive.

ex.en: Strife is the rock on which the party split.
ex.ja: 内紛が党の分裂したもとです。

ex.en: Marriage, in peace, is this world's paradise; in strife, this life's purgatory.
ex.ja: 結婚生活は夫婦仲が良ければ天国であり、夫婦仲が悪ければこの世の地獄である。

en: A musical range or section higher than bass and lower than alto.
A person, instrument, or group that performs in the tenor (higher than bass and lower than alto) range.
Of or pertaining to the tenor part or range.

tenor.ety: From Middle English tenour, from Anglo-Norman tenour, from Old French tenor (“substance, contents, meaning, sense; tenor part in music”), from Latin tenor (“course, continuance; holder”), from teneō (“to hold”). In music, from the notion of the one who holds the melody, as opposed to the countertenor.

note.ja: ラテン語 tenor（保たれた進路）から。ten（保つ）。旋律を保つ声部 →「テノール」、話の流れ →「趣旨」。

en: The characteristic of using a minimum of something (especially money).
A savings bank.
To shop or browse at a thrift shop; to buy (something) at a thrift shop.

thrift.ety: From Middle English thrift, thryfte, þrift, from Old Norse þrift (“thriving condition, prosperity”). Equivalent to thrive + -t.

ex.en: I bought it at a thrift shop.
ex.ja: リサイクルショップで買ったんです。

ex.en: A small income obliges us to thrift.
ex.ja: 収入が低いと倹約せざるを得なくなる。

ex.en: The speaker stressed the need for thrift.
ex.ja: 講演者は節約の必要を強調した。

en: A route used in mountaineering, specifically rock climbing, in which the descent occurs by a different route than the ascent.
A series of points, with angles and distances measured between, traveled around a subject, usually for use as "control" i.e. angular refe…
To travel across, to go through, to pass through, particularly under difficult conditions.
To visit all parts of; to explore thoroughly.
athwart; across; crosswise
Lying across; being in a direction across something else.

traverse.ety: From Middle English traversen, from Old French traverser, from Latin trans (“across”) + versus (“turned”), perfect passive participle of Latin vertere (“to turn”).

ex.en: The train traversed a tunnel.
ex.ja: 汽車はトンネルを通り抜けた。

note.ja: tra（= trans 越えて）+ vers（向ける）+ e。横切って向かう →「横断する・越える」。

en: A reproductive organ of therian mammals in which the young are conceived and develop until birth.
A similar part in some non-mammals.

uterus.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *úd
Proto-Indo-European *-teros
Proto-Indo-European *úderos
Latin uteruslbor.
English uterus
Learned borrowing from Latin uterus.

ex.en: How do babies breathe when they're in the uterus?
ex.ja: 赤ちゃんは子宮内で呼吸はどうしてるのですか？

en: A singer; a person who likes to sing.

vocalist.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Indo-European *wṓkʷs
Proto-Italic *wōks
Latin vōx
Proto-Indo-European *h₂el-
Proto-Indo-European *-is
Proto-Indo-European *h₂élisder.?
Proto-Italic *-ālis
Latin -ālis
Latin vōcālisbor.
Middle English vocal
English vocal
Proto-Indo-European *-id-
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-idyéti
Proto-Hellenic *-íd͏̌d͏̌ō

Proto-Hellenic *-tās
Ancient Greek -τής (-tḗs)
Ancient Greek -ῐστής (-ĭstḗs)bor.
Latin -istader.
Old French -istebor.
Middle English -ist
English -ist
English vocalist
From vocal + -ist.

ex.en: He is bent on becoming a vocalist.
ex.ja: 彼は声楽家になろうと決心している。

note.ja: voc（声）+ al + ist（人）。声で表現する人 →「歌手・ボーカリスト」。

en: Felis silvestris, a common small Old World wild cat somewhat larger than a house cat.
A bobcat (Lynx rufus) or other similar New World species of lynx.
Of or concerning customized or hand-made cartridges.
Unauthorized by the proper authorities.
To drill for oil in an area where no oil has been found before.

wildcat.ety:
From Middle English wyld cat, wylde cat (in the plural as wild cattes, wylde catis, wyle cattes), equivalent to wild + cat. Cognate with Middle Low German wiltkatte, German Wildkatze, Swedish vildkatt.
Its adjectival senses were originally American and derived from the "wildcat banks" of Michigan, following its elevation to statehood in 1837. Two laws—one easing the requirements for establishing a new bank and another occasioned by the Panic of 1837 that removed the need for payment in specie—led to the creation and collapse of around 50 banks within two years. The term is apocryphally derived

en: An artificial method of preventing sensation, used to eliminate pain without causing loss of vital functions, by the administration of on…
The loss or prevention of sensation, as caused by anesthesia (in the above sense), or by a lesion in the nervous system, or by another ph…

anesthesia.ety:
Sense of “insensibility” attested since 1679, from New Latin anaesthēsia, from Ancient Greek ἀναισθησία (anaisthēsía, “without sensation”), from ἀν- (an-, “not”) and αἴσθησις (aísthēsis, “sensation”). By surface analysis, an- + -esthesia.
Sense of “state induced by an agent” attested since 1846.

ex.en: He was put under anesthesia.
ex.ja: 彼は麻酔をかけられた。

ex.en: I'll give you anaesthesia.
ex.ja: 麻酔の注射をします。

ex.en: The hospital patient dropped off shortly after the doctor injected him with anesthesia.
ex.ja: 入院患者は医者に麻酔を注射されてすぐに眠りに落ちた。

en: The quality or state of being anonymous (nameless or unidentified).
That which is anonymous.

anonymity.ety: From Latin anonymus or its etymon Ancient Greek ἀνώνυμος (anṓnumos, “anonymous”) + -ity. Compare French anonymité.

ex.en: Anonymity or detailed reference are both fine.
ex.ja: 匿名でも、詳細な情報を書いて頂いても、どちらでも結構です。

ex.en: The government official spoke to the reporter on condition of anonymity.
ex.ja: その官僚は匿名を条件として記者に話をした。

en: An act or instance of appropriating.
That which is appropriated.

appropriation.ety: From Middle English appropriacion, appropriacioun, from Medieval Latin appropriātiō. By surface analysis, appropriate + -ion.

ex.en: Reproduction or appropriation of HTML, images and photographs from within this site is prohibited.
ex.ja: 本サイト内の記述、画像、写真の無断転載・転用を禁止します。

en: A musical piece written typically for a solo voice with orchestral accompaniment in an opera or cantata.

From Italian aria, metathesis from Latin āerem, accusative of āēr, from Ancient Greek ἀήρ (aḗr, “air”). Doublet of air.

ex.en: The third aria is the part in which she makes herself heard the best.
ex.ja: 第３幕のアリアが彼女の一番の聴かせどころだ。

en: To murder someone, especially an important person, by a sudden or obscure attack, especially for ideological or political reasons.
To harm, ruin, or defame severely or destroy by treachery, slander, libel, or obscure attack.

assassinate.ety: From assassin + -ate, after Middle French assassiner.

ex.en: They attempted to assassinate the president.
ex.ja: 彼らは大統領の暗殺を企てた。

ex.en: He was ignorant of the plot to assassinate him.
ex.ja: 彼は自分を暗殺しようという陰謀を知らなかった。

ex.en: The great Roman hero, Julius Caesar, was assassinated.
ex.ja: かのローマの偉大な英雄、ジュリアス・シーザーは暗殺されたのです。

en: One who robs others in a lawless area, especially as part of a group.
An outlaw.
To rob, or steal from, in the manner of a bandit.

bandit.ety: Borrowed from Italian bandito (“outlawed”), a derivative of Italian bandire (“to ban”), from Late Latin bandīre, an alteration (due to Gothic 𐌱𐌰𐌽𐌳𐍅𐌾𐌰𐌽 (bandwjan, “to signal”)) of Late Latin bannīre (“to ban”), from Frankish *bannan (“to ban”). Doublet of bandito.

ex.en: The bandits demanded all money in the register.
ex.ja: 悪漢は金銭登録機のお金を要求した。

ex.en: The bandits made a raid on the village.
ex.ja: 山賊がその村を襲った。

en: Wearing nothing on the feet.
Of a vehicle on an icy road: not using snow chains.
Wearing nothing on the feet.
Transmitting without the use of an amplifier.

barefoot.ety: From Middle English barefote, barfot, from Old English bærfōt (“barefoot”), from Proto-West Germanic *baʀafōt, from Proto-Germanic *bazafōts (“barefoot”) equivalent to bare + foot. Cognate with Scots barefit (“barefoot”), Old Frisian berfōt ("barefoot"; modern Saterland Frisian boarfouts (“barefoot”, adverb)), Dutch barrevoets (“barefoot”, adverb), German barfuß (“barefoot”), Danish barfodet (“barefoot”), Swedish barfota (“barefoot”, adverb), Icelandic berfættur (“barefoot”), Yiddish באָרוועס (borves, “barefoot”).

ex.en: I'm always barefoot at home.
ex.ja: 家ではいつも裸足です。

ex.en: I can't walk barefoot.
ex.ja: 裸足では歩けません。

ex.en: Why are you barefoot?
ex.ja: どうして裸足なの？

en: An artificial obstruction, such as a dam, in a river designed to increase its depth or to divert its flow.
A heavy curtain of artillery fire directed in front of one's own troops to screen and protect them.
To direct a barrage at.

barrage.ety: Unadapted borrowing from French barrage (“barrage, barrier”) c. 1859. Compare barrier.

ex.en: The minister had to face a barrage of questions from the press.
ex.ja: 大臣は新聞記者たちからの矢継ぎ早の質問に直面しなくてはならなかった。

en: To apply or make use of (someone or something); to employ, to use.
To impart (something) gratuitously; to present (something) to someone or something, especially as a gift or an honour; to confer, to give…

bestow.ety:
PIE word
 *h₁épi
The verb is derived from Middle English bestowen, bistouen, bistowen (“to give, bestow; to apply (something to something else); to arrange or have control over (something); to place (someone) in a position; to use (for some purpose); (reflexive) to find (oneself) a place to live or shelter”) [and other forms], from bi- (prefix forming verbs, often with a completive, figurative, or intensive meaning) + stouen, stowen (“to pack (cargo) in a ship, stow; to place (someone) in a certain position; to provide quarters for, lodge; etc.”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- (“

ex.en: They bestowed several gifts on the royal visitors.
ex.ja: 彼らは王室からの訪問者に贈り物を幾つか渡した。

ex.en: He who gives to another bestows on himself.
ex.ja: 情けは人のためならず。

ex.en: The committee bestowed a medal on him.
ex.ja: 委員会は彼にメダルを授けた。

en: The quality of being exceptionally effulgent (giving off light).
The quality of having extraordinary mental capacity.

ex.en: Every time I saw him, I was overcome with his brilliance.
ex.ja: 彼に会うたびごとに、彼の頭の良さに圧倒された。

en: Water in which food (meat, vegetable, etc.) has been boiled.
A soup made from broth and other ingredients such as vegetables, herbs or diced meat.

broth.ety: From Middle English broth, from Old English broþ (“broth”), from Proto-West Germanic *broþ (“broth”), from Proto-Germanic *bruþą (“broth”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰrewh₁- (“to seethe, roil, brew”). By surface analysis, brew + -th (abstract nominal suffix).

ex.en: The broth is hot.
ex.ja: そのスープ熱いよ。

ex.en: You're right. The noodle broth here is a bit expensive.
ex.ja: その通りさ。ここの麺の出汁はちょっと値が張るんだ。

ex.en: Too many cooks spoil the broth.
ex.ja: 料理人が多すぎるとスープができそこなう。

en: A point or place where a check is performed, especially a point along a road or on a frontier where travellers are stopped for inspection.
A situation, often represented by a point in time, at which the state of a database system is known to be valid, and to which it can be r…
To set a checkpoint.

ex.en: There's a checkpoint at the border where they look in your trunk.
ex.ja: その国境には、トランクの中身を見るチェックポイントがある。

ex.en: The coalition force fired at her car at the checkpoint in Baghdad.
ex.ja: 同盟軍はバグダッドの検問所で彼女の車を襲撃した。

en: Any binary compound of chlorine and another element or radical.
Any salt of hydrochloric acid.

chloride.ety: From chlor(ine) + -ide, coined by British chemist Humphry Davy in 1812.

en: to identify by or divide into classes; to categorize
to declare something a secret, especially a government secret

classify.ety: From French classifier. By surface analysis, class + -ify.

ex.en: Please classify these books by subject.
ex.ja: これらの本を主題別に分類してください。

ex.en: One can classify books into good ones and bad ones.
ex.ja: 本は良い物と悪い物とに分類できる。

ex.en: I classify his music as rock.
ex.ja: 私は彼の音楽をロックに入れる。

zh: 太過自信的 /太过自信的

en: Overly confident; arrogant and boastful.
A familiar name for a cockatoo.
To operate a small-scale farm.

cocky.ety: From cock (“male domestic chicken”) + -y (suffix forming adjectives with the sense of ‘having the quality of’).

ex.en: You cocky little kid!
ex.ja: 生意気な小僧がよ。

en: Cooperating.
A constant by which an algebraic term is multiplied.
An entry of a matrix.

coefficient.ety: From French coefficient. Coined by French mathematician François Viète. Or influenced by (New) Latin coefficient-, which is the stem of coefficiens, which is a substantivation of the present active participle of coefficio, which comes from co- and efficio.

en: A cluster of heterogeneous things.
A corporation formed by the combination of several smaller corporations whose activities are unrelated to the corporation's primary activ…
Clustered together into a mass.
Composed of fragments of rock, pebbles, or stones cemented together.
To combine together into a larger mass.
To combine together into a larger corporation.

conglomerate.ety: First attested in the second part of the 16ᵗʰ century; from Latin conglomerātus, perfect passive participle of conglomerō (“to pile into a heap, to roll together”) (see -ate (Etymology 1, 2 and 3)), from con- (prefix indicating a being or bringing together of several objects) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱóm (“beside, by, near, with”)) + glomerāre (from glomerō (“to pile into a heap, to make into a ball, glomerate”), from glomus (“ball of thread; ball-shaped mass”), from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to form into a ball; ball”)).

en: A stone forming the base at the corner of a building.
Such a stone used ceremonially, often inscribed with the architect's and owner's names, dates and other details.

cornerstone.ety: From Middle English corner ston; equivalent to corner + stone. The figurative sense is in part after Psalm 118:22, and is also quoted several times in the New Testament.

en: False, especially of money; intended to deceive or carry appearance of being genuine.
Inauthentic.
A non-genuine article; a fake.
One who counterfeits; a counterfeiter.
To falsely produce what appears to be official or valid; to produce a forged copy of.
Of a turn or river card, to invalidate a player's hand by making a better hand on the board.

counterfeit.ety: From Middle English counterfeit, countrefet, from Anglo-Norman countrefait, from Old French contrefait, from Latin contra- (“against”) + Latin facere (“to make”). Piecewise doublet of contrafactum.

ex.en: The counterfeit bills flooded the market over the weekend.
ex.ja: 週末に偽札が市場にあふれた。

note.ja: counter（反対に・対応して）+ feit（作る）。ラテン語 contrafacere（まねて作る）から →「偽造の・偽物」。fac と同じ。

en: Extremely bright, especially so as to blind the eyes temporarily; bright to the degree that dazzles.
Very brilliant or splendid in display; that dazzles the mind of the observer.
The action of the verb to dazzle; dazzlement

ex.en: Your eyes are like corals, dazzling and very pretty.
ex.ja: 君の目はまるでサンゴのよう。ギラギラしていて、とてもきれい。

ex.en: The sun is dazzling.
ex.ja: 太陽がまぶしい。

ex.en: The noonday sun beat down with dazzling brightness on the tennis court.
ex.ja: 真昼の太陽がテニスコートを目も眩むほどに照らしあげた。

en: A designated minister of charity in the early Church (see Acts 6:1-6).
A clergyman ranked directly below a priest, with duties of helping the priests and carrying out parish work.
To ordain to the diaconate.
For a choir leader to lead a hymn by speaking one or two lines at a time, which are then sung by the choir.

deacon.ety: Inherited from Middle English deken, dekne, from Old English diacon, from Ecclesiastical Latin diāconus, from Ancient Greek διᾱ́κονος (diā́konos, “servant, minister”).

en: To trick or mislead.

deceive.ety: From Middle English deceyven, from Anglo-Norman deceivre, from Latin dēcipiō (“to deceive; beguile; entrap”), from dē- (“from”) + capiō (“to seize”); see captive. Compare conceive, perceive, receive. Displaced native Old English beswīcan.

ex.en: Try it I think you will be deceived.
ex.ja: 騙されたと思ってやってみて。

ex.en: The boy I thought was honest deceived me.
ex.ja: 正直だと思っていた少年が私をだました。

ex.en: He is the last man to deceive me.
ex.ja: 彼は決して私をだますような人間ではない。

note.ja: de（離れて）+ ceiv（つかむ）+ e。（人の判断を）つかんで離さない →「だます・欺く」。deception（欺き）。

en: The field of medicine concerned with the study, diagnosis, and treatment of conditions of the teeth and oral cavity.
Operations performed on teeth and adjoining areas such as drilling, filling cavities, and placing crowns and bridges.

en: A brief extra performance, done after the main performance is complete.
A call or demand (as by continued applause) for a repeat performance.
Please perform again!
To call for an extra performance or repetition of, or by.
To call for an encore.

encore.ety: Borrowed from French encore (“more, again”), and once used in this sense.

ex.en: Everyone called out to the singer for an encore.
ex.ja: 歌手に向かって盛んなアンコールが起こった。

ex.en: The pianist played two encores.
ex.ja: そのピアニストはアンコールに応えて２曲弾いた。

en: To make a mistake.
To sin.
Elongated form of er (“sound of hesitation”).

err.ety: From Middle English erren, from Old French errer (“to wander, err, mistake”), from Latin errō (“wander, stray, err, mistake”, verb), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ers- (“to be angry, lose one's temper”). Cognate with Old English eorre, ierre (“anger, wrath, ire”), Old English iersian (“to be angry with, rage, irritate, provoke”), Old English ierre (“wandering, gone astray, confused”).

ex.en: He that thinks little, errs much.
ex.ja: あまり考えない者が、多くの過ちをおかす。

ex.en: He that talks much, errs much.
ex.ja: 多弁の人は多く誤る。

ex.en: He erred on the side of severity.
ex.ja: 彼は厳格すぎた。

en: To eject something violently (such as lava or water, as from a volcano or geyser).
To burst forth; to break out.

erupt.ety: From Latin eruptus, past participle of ērumpō (“to break out (of), to burst out (from)”), from e (“out”) + rumpō (“to break”).

ex.en: The volcano erupted suddenly, killing many people.
ex.ja: その火山は突然噴火し、多くの人が亡くなった。

ex.en: The volcano has erupted twice this year.
ex.ja: その火山は今年２度噴火した。

ex.en: The volcano may erupt at any moment.
ex.ja: その火山はいつなんどき爆発するかもしれない。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ rupt（破る）。破って外へ出る →「噴火する・爆発する」。

en: A concentrated coffee beverage brewed by forcing hot water under high pressure through finely ground coffee.
A drink that includes espresso as an ingredient.

espresso.ety:
Borrowed from Italian espresso, from caffè espresso (“pressed-out coffee”), form of esprimere (“to press out”), from Latin exprimere, from ex- (“out”) + primere (“to press”).
Some sources derive the term from "expressly" ("individually, directly") made for the customer, or from the Italian espresso ("fast"), as in the English word express ("fast"), although these explanations are not widely accepted. The original term for modern espresso (coffee extracted under pressure) was cream coffee, from Italian caffè crema (variant: crema caffè), due to the crema, and appeared on early Gaggia machines,

ex.en: An espresso doppio to drink inside.
ex.ja: エスプレッソドピオ店内で。

ex.en: I drank a very hot double espresso at the coffee shop this morning.
ex.ja: 今朝、コーヒーショップでとても熱いダブルエスプレッソを飲んだ。

en: To get away from by cunning; to avoid by using dexterity, subterfuge, address, or ingenuity; to cleverly escape from.
To escape; to slip away; — sometimes with from.

evade.ety: From Middle French évader, from Latin ēvādō (“to pass or go over; flee”), from ē (“out of, from”) + vādō (“to go; walk”). See also wade.

ex.en: Jack tried to evade paying his taxes.
ex.ja: ジャックは脱税しようとした。

ex.en: He was accused of evading tax.
ex.ja: 彼は脱税で非難された。

ex.en: We won't be able to evade punishment this time.
ex.ja: 今度は罰をまぬがれまい。

en: Incapable of producing results, useless; doomed not to be successful; not worth attempting.
Insignificant; frivolous.

futile.ety: Borrowed from Middle French futile, from Latin fūtilis.

ex.en: It isn't futile to go to university.
ex.ja: 大学へ行くことは無駄ではない。

note.ja: ラテン語 futilis（漏れやすい）から。fundere（注ぐ）の仲間。注いでもこぼれる →「無駄な・むなしい」。

en: The embryo of a seed, especially of a seed used as a cereal or grain. See Wikipedia article on cereal germ.
The small mass of cells from which a part of an organism develops, or a macroscopic but immature form of that part; a bud.
To germinate.

germ.ety: From Middle French germe, from Latin germen (“bud, seed, embryo”). Doublet of germen.

ex.en: Germs are too tiny for our eyes to see.
ex.ja: 細菌は小さすぎて我々の眼には見えない。

ex.en: This milk is free from germs.
ex.ja: この牛乳は殺菌してある。

ex.en: This chemical will prevent germs from breeding.
ex.ja: この化学薬品は細菌の繁殖を防ぐだろう。

en: A specialized cell, group of cells, or organ of endothelial origin in the human or animal body that synthesizes a chemical substance, suc…
A structure resembling a gland, especially a lymph node.

gland.ety: Late 17th century borrowing from French glande, alteration of Old French glandre, from Latin glandulae (“throat glands, tonsils”), plural of glandula (“a little acorn”), from glāns (“an acorn”) + -ula (diminutive nominal suffix).

en: Not very illuminated; dim because of darkness, especially when appearing depressing or frightening.
Suffering from gloom; melancholy; dejected.
Someone or something that is gloomy or pessimistic.

gloomy.ety: From gloom + -y. Cognate with Saterland Frisian glumig (“dark, gloomy”).

ex.en: I got gloomy and thought of giving up.
ex.ja: 私は落ち込んでしまいあきらめようかと思った。

ex.en: The room was gloomy and cold.
ex.ja: 部屋は薄暗くてひんやりしていた。

ex.en: There are a lot of gloomy sentences today.
ex.ja: 今日は、悲観的な文章が多いね。

en: Having or showing grace in movement, shape, or proportion.
Magnanimous, lacking arrogance or complaint; gracious.

graceful.ety: From Middle English graceful. By surface analysis, grace + -ful.

ex.en: How can I say things to sound graceful?
ex.ja: どう言えば、おしとやかに聞こえる？

ex.en: She is beautiful, and what is more, very graceful.
ex.ja: 彼女は美しいが、さらによいことには非常に上品だ。

ex.en: The lady has a graceful manner.
ex.ja: その婦人の態度はしとやかだ。

en: Something which causes grief.
A wrong or hardship suffered, which is the grounds of a complaint.

grievance.ety: From Old French grievance, from the verb grever (“to irritate; to bother; to annoy”) + -ance, equivalent to grieve + -ance.

en: Overwhelming mental anguish or grief, especially that caused by loss or disappointment.

heartbreak.ety: From heart + break. Compare heartache § Etymology.

ex.en: It's not that I particularly love heartbreak, but I really like songs about heartbreak.
ex.ja: 別に失恋が好きなわけじゃないけど、失恋ソングはすごく好きなんだよね。

en: A member of a fictional race of small humanoids with shaggy hair and hairy feet.
A person of short stature.

hobbit.ety: Coined in its current sense by J. R. R. Tolkien in the 1930s, featured in the novels The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings. Jocularly etymologized by him as from a hypothetical Old English *holbytla (literally “hole-builder”), from hol (“hole”) + bytlan (“to build”) + -a (“-er”). Tolkien was possibly influenced by similar terms for house-sprites (probably from Hob, a hypocoristic form of Robert), or an isolated mention of hobbits (with hobgoblins following immediately afterwards) in a list of sprites and bogies from the 19th-century Denham Tracts.

en: The back of a horse.
A ridge of sand, gravel, and boulders.
On the back of a horse.

horseback.ety: From Middle English horsebacke, horsebak, horsbak, equivalent to horse + back.

ex.en: A man on horseback came along the path.
ex.ja: 男が馬に乗ってその道をやってきた。

ex.en: He likes to go out on horseback.
ex.ja: 彼は馬に乗って出かけるのが好きです。

ex.en: I'd like to try horseback riding.
ex.ja: 乗馬をしたいのですが。

en: The provision of palliative care for terminally ill patients, either at a specialized facility or at a residence, and support for the fam…
A specialized facility or organization offering palliative care for the terminally ill.

hospice.ety: Borrowed from French hospice, from Old French hospise, from Latin hospitium (“hospitality, an inn”). Doublet of hospitium.

en: A telephone line that is always staffed and able to give immediate assistance.
A direct line between two people, especially one between heads of state to be used in an emergency.
To communicate over a telephone hotline.

en: The act of inhibiting.
A personal feeling of fear or embarrassment that stops one behaving naturally.

inhibition.ety:
From Middle English inhibicioun, inhibicione from Old French inibicion, from Latin inhibitio.
Morphologically inhibit + -ion.

ex.en: Tom is truly free from inhibition.
ex.ja: トムって、本当に自由奔放ね。

ex.en: Tom lies without any inhibition.
ex.ja: トムは平気で嘘をつく。

en: A number that is not a fraction; an element of the infinite and numerable set {..., -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...}.

integer.ety: Borrowed from Latin integer (“whole”), from Proto-Italic *n̥tagros (“untouched”). Doublet of entier and entire. Related to English tact, thack, and thwack.

note.ja: ラテン語 integer（触れられていない→完全な）から。in（否定）+ teg（触れる）。欠けのない数 →「整数」。integrity（完全性・誠実さ）も同じ。

en: Of or pertaining to multiple distinct academic disciplines or fields of study.
Of or pertaining to a linkage between multiple distinct academic disciplines or fields of study.

Proto-Indo-European *h₁n̥tér

English disciplinary

From inter- + disciplinary.

en: Stopping and starting, occurring, or presenting at intervals; coming after a particular time span.
Existing only for certain seasons; that is, being dry for part of the year.

intermittent.ety: From Middle French intermittent, from Latin intermittens (“sending between”), from prefix inter- (“among, on”) + mittens (“sending”), from mittere (“to send”).

ex.en: It's been intermittent for 2 or 3 months.
ex.ja: 断続的ですが、もう２、３ヶ月になります。

en: The act of making timid or fearful or of deterring by threats; the state of being intimidated.

intimidation.ety: From intimidate + -ion. Compare French intimidation; perhaps modeled on it.

en: A precept; a succinct statement or observation of a rule of conduct or moral teaching.

maxim.ety: From Anglo-Norman maxime and Middle French maxime, from Late Latin maxima (“axiom”), noun use of the feminine singular form of Latin maximus (apparently as used in the phrase prōpositiō maxima (“greatest premise”)). Doublet of maxima.

ex.en: He worked in his favorite maxim.
ex.ja: 彼は自分のすきな格言をいれた。

note.ja: ラテン語 maxima（最大の命題）から。max（最大）。最も重要な言葉 →「格言・金言」。

en: Black bile, formerly thought to be one of the four "cardinal humours" of animal bodies.
Great sadness or depression, especially of a thoughtful or introspective nature.
Affected with great sadness or depression.
Suggestive of wistfulness or subdued emotion.

melancholy.ety: From Middle English malencolie, from Old French melancolie, from Ancient Greek μελαγχολία (melankholía, “atrabiliousness”) (from μέλας (mélas), μελαν- (melan-, “black, dark, murky”) + χολή (kholḗ, “bile”)), referring to the humour which ancient Hippocratic and later Galenic medicine associated with sadness and despondency. Compare the Latin ātra bīlis (“black bile”). The adjectival use is a Middle English innovation, perhaps influenced by the suffixes -y, -ly. Doublet of melancholia.

ex.en: Her words were filled with melancholy.
ex.ja: 彼女の言葉は憂鬱に満ちていた。

ex.en: We sensed a melancholy note in his voice.
ex.ja: 彼の声には憂鬱な調子が感じられた。

ex.en: He was overcome by a feeling of melancholy.
ex.ja: 彼は憂うつな感情に打ちのめされた。

en: Covered in mist; foggy.
Dim; vague; obscure.

misty.ety: From Middle English misty, mysty, misti, from Old English mistiġ (“misty, dark”), from Proto-West Germanic *mistig (“misty”), equivalent to mist + -y. Cognate with Scots misty, mistie (“misty”), West Frisian mistich (“misty, foggy”), Dutch mistig (“misty, foggy”), German Low German mistig (“foggy”).

ex.en: It was cold and misty.
ex.ja: 寒くて霧がかかっていた。

ex.en: The girl disappeared in the misty forest.
ex.ja: その女の子が霧たちこめる森の中でなくなっちまった。

ex.en: I think that Misty has different feelings towards insects.
ex.ja: ミスティーさんは虫について違う感情があると思う。

en: An implement for washing floors or similar, made of a piece of cloth, or a collection of thrums, or coarse yarn, fastened to a handle.
A wash with a mop; the act of mopping.
To rub, scrub, clean or wipe with a mop, or as if with a mop.

mop.ety: From Middle English mappe (also as mappel), perhaps borrowed from Walloon mappe (“napkin”), from Latin mappa (“napkin, cloth”). Believed to be from a Semitic source, variously claimed as Phoenician or Punic (the latter by Quintilian). Compare Modern Hebrew מַפָּה (mapá, “a map; a cloth”) (shortened from מַנְפָּה (manpah, “fluttering banner, streaming cloth”)). Doublet of map, nape, and nappe.

ex.en: I promise I'll mop the floor tomorrow morning.
ex.ja: 明日の朝、床のモップがけをするって約束するよ。

ex.en: Have you mopped the kitchen floor yet?
ex.ja: 台所の床のモップ掛けって、もうやった？

ex.en: Have you already mopped the kitchen floor?
ex.ja: 台所の床のモップ掛けって、もうやった？

en: Able to be neglected, ignored or excluded from consideration; too small or unimportant to be of concern.

negligible.ety: From negligence/negligent + -ible, as if from New Latin *negligibilis, from Latin neglegō (“to neglect”) + -ibilis (“-ible”).

ex.en: The damage from the flood was negligible.
ex.ja: 洪水の被害はごくわずかだった。

note.ja: neg（否定）+ lig（拾う・選ぶ）+ ible。拾い上げなくてもよい →「取るに足りない・ごくわずかな」。neglect（無視する）。

en: The state or quality of being without clothing on the body; specifically, the quality of being without clothing on the genitals.

nudity.ety: From nude + -ity. Compare Late Latin nūditās.

en: An element of decoration; that which embellishes or adorns.
Christmas ornament: a Christmas tree decoration.
To decorate.
To add to.

ornament.ety: From Middle English ornament, from Old French ornement, from Latin ornamentum (“equipment, apparatus, furniture, trappings, adornment, embellishment”), from ornāre (“to equip, adorn”). The verb is derived from the noun.

ex.en: It is merely an ornament.
ex.ja: それは飾りにすぎない。

ex.en: The bedroom was laden with beautiful ornaments.
ex.ja: その寝室には、美しい装飾品がいっぱいあった。

ex.en: The room is richly ornamented.
ex.ja: その部屋は装飾を凝らしている。

en: The spillage resultant from overflowing.
An outlet for escape of excess material.
To flow over the brim of (a container).
To cover with a liquid, literally or figuratively.

overflow.ety: From Middle English overflowen, from Old English oferflōwan, equivalent to over- + flow.

ex.en: This river looks like it's going to overflow.
ex.ja: この川は氾濫しそうだ。

ex.en: The river overflowed because of the heavy rain.
ex.ja: 大雨で川があふれた。

ex.en: The stadium was overflowing with people.
ex.ja: スタディアムは溢れんばかりの人込みだった。

en: The combination of a substance with oxygen.
A reaction in which the atoms of an element lose electrons and the oxidation state of the element increases.

oxidation.ety: From French oxydation, equivalent to oxide + -ation. See oxidate.

en: An unbroken view of an entire surrounding area.
A picture or series of pictures representing a continuous scene.

panorama.ety:
From pan- (“all”) + Ancient Greek ὅρᾱμᾰ (hórāmă, “view”).
Coined by Robert Barker (painter) in 1792.

ex.en: The hill commands the panorama of the city.
ex.ja: この丘から市の全景がよく見える。

en: In the International System of Units, the derived unit of pressure and stress; one newton per square metre. Symbol: Pa.

pascal.ety: Borrowed from French pascal, named after French scientist and philosopher Blaise Pascal. Doublet of Paschal.

ex.en: The examples used in this article make use of a Pascal-like pseudocode.
ex.ja: この記事で扱う例は、Pascal言語に似た疑似コードを使用しています。

en: A cucumber preserved in a solution, usually a brine or a vinegar syrup.
Any vegetable preserved in vinegar and consumed as relish.
To preserve food (or sometimes other things) in a salt, sugar or vinegar solution.
To remove high-temperature scale and oxidation from metal with heated (often sulphuric) industrial acid.

pickle.ety: From Middle English pikel (“spicy sauce served with meat or fish”), borrowed from Middle Dutch, Middle Low German pekel (“brine”). Cognate with Scots pikkill (“salt liquor, brine”), Saterland Frisian Piekele (“pickle, brine”), Dutch pekel (“pickle, brine”), Low German pekel, peckel, pickel, bickel (“pickle, brine”), German Pökel (“pickle, brine”), Icelandic pækill (“brine”).

ex.en: The pickled radish needs a touch of salt.
ex.ja: この沢庵は塩気が足りない。

ex.en: Our granny is an expert at pickling foods.
ex.ja: うちのおばあちゃん、漬物名人なのよ。

ex.en: We ordered a pizza with potatoes and pickles.
ex.ja: ポテトとピクルス入りのピザを注文しました。

en: Pinkish.
A baby mouse, especially when used as food for a snake, etc.
The Australasian snapper or pink snapper (Chrysophrys auratus).

ex.ja: 薬指を曲げずに、小指だけを曲げれる？

en: A writer and creator of theatrical plays.

ex.en: A student visited the house of the great playwright.
ex.ja: 学生が偉大な劇作家の家を訪問した。

ex.en: I am determined to make a living as a playwright.
ex.ja: 僕は脚本家で食べていく決心をした。

ex.en: I am determined to make a living as a playwright at all costs.
ex.ja: わたしはどんな犠牲を払っても、脚本家で食べていくと心にきめている。

en: Of, or relating to a predator.
Living by preying on other living animals.

predatory.ety: Borrowed from Latin praedātōrius, equivalent to predator + -y.

en: A beginning or introductory portion that comes before the main text of a document or book, typically serving to contextualize or explain …
An introduction, or series of preliminary remarks.
To introduce or make a comment before (the main point); to premise.
To give a preface to.

preface.ety: Late 14th century, from Middle English preface, prefas, from Old French preface (from which derives the modern French préface), from Medieval Latin prefātia, for classical Latin praefātiō (“a saying beforehand”), from praefor (“to speak beforehand”), from prae- (“beforehand”) + for (“to speak”).

ex.en: He wrote a fine preface to the play.
ex.ja: 彼はその戯曲にすばらしい序文を書いた。

ex.en: He said a few words by way of preface.
ex.ja: 彼は前置きとして、すこし話した。

ex.en: How does the preface run?
ex.ja: 序文にはなんと書いてありますか。

en: To order (a drug or medical device) for use by a particular patient (under licensed authority).
To specify by writing as a required procedure or ritual; to lay down authoritatively as a guide, direction, or rule of action.

ex.ja: この犯罪に対して法律はある罰則が規定されている。

ex.en: I'll prescribe some antibiotics.
ex.ja: 抗生物質を処方しましょう。

en: A forest in a climate with high annual rainfall and no dry season.

rainforest.ety: From rain + forest, a calque of German Regenwald.

ex.en: Rainforests provide the earth with many benefits.
ex.ja: 熱帯雨林は地球に多くの恩恵を与える。

ex.en: The destruction of the rainforests affects our environment.
ex.ja: 熱帯雨林の破壊は環境に影響を及ぼす。

ex.en: More than 90 percent of Madagascar's rainforests have been destroyed.
ex.ja: マダガスカルの熱帯林の９０％以上が伐採されました。

en: Revived or regenerated, especially emotionally or spiritually.
Reincarnated.
A manufactured vinyl doll that has been transformed to resemble a human baby with as much realism as possible.

ex.ja: もしも私が生まれ変わるなら、鳥になりたい。

ex.en: I want to be reborn as a Canadian if I had the chance.
ex.ja: 生まれ変わったらカナダ人になりたい。

ex.en: If I were reborn, I would want to learn the violin.
ex.ja: 生まれ変わったらヴァイオリン習いたい。

en: A book, pamphlet or other printed matter that has been published once before but is now being released again.
To print (something) that has been published in print before.
To renew the impression of.

ex.en: Is it possible to reprint this article?
ex.ja: この記事を転載することは可能でしょうか。

ex.en: Is reprinting this article a possibility?
ex.ja: この記事を転載することは可能でしょうか。

en: A room containing a public toilet: a public lavatory.

restroom.ety: From rest + room, from an earlier sense of "breakroom".

ex.en: Can you tell me where the restroom is?
ex.ja: お手洗いはどこか教えて下さいませんか。

ex.en: There was a long line for the women's restroom.
ex.ja: 女性用トイレは長蛇の列だった。

ex.en: There was a long line for the women's restrooms.
ex.ja: 女性用トイレは長蛇の列だった。

en: A game of chance in which a small ball is made to move round rapidly on a circle divided off into numbered (usually red and black) spaces…
An instance of risk-taking, especially when the downside exceeds the upside (contrary to the game of roulette where only the wager is lost).
To separate or decorate by incisions made with a small toothed wheel.

roulette.ety: Borrowed from French roulette (“roulette, little wheel”). The sense "situation with a random chance of incurring serious harm" may be abstracted from Russian roulette.
